item.description: We have just come through a season of words.

item.title: The Government That Stays
item.description: The ballots are in, the posters are coming down, and the talks have barely started.

item.title: After Which Things? Four Readings of One Phrase
item.description: The Akeida, read on Shabbat 31 October 2026, opens with four words that have kept commentators busy for a thousand years: "וַיְהִי אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה".

item.title: The Treaty Before the Test
item.description: On Friday 30 October 2026 the sixth aliyah of Vayera closes at Be'er Sheva.

item.title: Here I Am: The Akeida and the Families of Israel
item.description: On Shabbat, 31 October 2026, we read the Akeida.

item.title: A Well, Seven Ewes and a Tamarisk
item.description: The sixth aliyah of Vayera, read on Friday 30 October 2026, is a short scene of diplomacy.

item.title: From Notebooks to Ballots: Mediation, Simplest Interpretations, and National-Religious Political Behavior
item.description: An analysis of the multi-layered mediation from Rav Kook’s private notebooks to contemporary electoral practice.

item.title: Pray for Avimelech
item.description: The day after the vote, Avraham prays for the king who wronged him and asks for the very blessing his own house still lacks.

item.title: One in Nine Isn't Here
item.description: Why Israel's official turnout reads lower than the share of residents who vote. Tuesday 27 October 2026 / 16 Cheshvan 5787.

item.title: Twenty-Eight Seats and No Government
item.description: Why the party that comes first in Israel doesn't automatically form the government. For readers abroad. Tuesday 27 October 2026, after voting ended at 22:00.

item.title: Before Thursday Noon
item.description: Voting ends at 22:00 tonight. Within minutes the screens will fill with numbers, and half the country will decide it knows what happened. It doesn't yet. Tonight is the start of a count. The official answer comes later, and there is a reason for that.

item.title: The Line at 22:00
item.description: Why the voting hours should stay where they were set. Tuesday 27 October 2026 / 16 Cheshvan 5787.

item.title: 5.45 Million by Eight O'Clock
item.description: By 20:00, 74.3% of eligible Israelis had voted, compared with 66% at the same hour in 2022. That's 5,449,277 people, according to the Central Elections Committee.

item.title: 4.89 Million by Six O'Clock
item.description: The 18:00 turnout on election day, counted in people, and what Yitzchak did toward evening.

item.title: Seven and a Half Million Who?
item.description: A Belgian broadcaster says 7.5 million Palestinians can’t vote in today’s election. The number checks out. What’s missing is the more than a million Arab citizens who are voting today.

item.title: 4,085,075 by Four O'Clock
item.description: The 16:00 turnout on election day, counted in people, and what Avraham did in the heat of the day.

item.title: Where Does a Lost Vote Go?
item.description: What happens to the votes for a list that doesn't pass the threshold. Tuesday 27 October 2026 / 16 Cheshvan 5787.

item.title: As One Who Jests
item.description: Since early afternoon on election day, replies across X have said there's no point in voting because it's already decided. This week's parsha shows how a real warning gets heard as a joke.

item.title: 3,290,480 by Two O'Clock
item.description: The 14:00 turnout on election day, counted in people instead of percentages, and what Avraham's early morning says about the hours that are left.
